title: Units and what they measure
idea: Every quantity has its own unit, and some of the names look alike. Hertz is not henry, watts are not watt-hours.

rows: The push: a difference in voltage makes electrons flow

compare.how: Measures voltage, also called electric potential.
Inductance. Looks like hertz, but isn't.

traps.why: Watt-hours measure energy used over time. Power itself is in watts.
Voltage is the push. The flow of electrons is current.
Wavelength is the length of one wave. Cycles per second is frequency.
Henry is the unit of inductance. Frequency is in hertz.
Current is the flow. The rate energy is used is power.
Farad is capacitance. Inductance is the henry.
Despite the name, a potentiometer is not a meter. Electric potential (voltage) is measured with a voltmeter.
